name: Huntington's Disease
description: Huntington's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by an inherited defect in a single gene. It causes the progressive breakdown of nerve cells in the brain, affecting movement, cognitive abilities, and behavior.
ageOfOnset: Typically 30-50 years (juvenile form can occur before 20)
prognosis: Progressive deterioration over 10-25 years after symptom onset
diagnosticMethods: Genetic testing for CAG repeat expansion in HTT gene
keyResearchCenters: UCL Queen Square Institute of Neurology
University of British Columbia HD Clinic
eli5Summary: Huntington's disease happens when a part of a gene repeats too many times. This causes brain cells to slowly stop working, which makes it hard for people to control their movements, remember things, and manage their feelings. Scientists are working hard to find ways to stop the disease.
clinicalSummary: Huntington's disease is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder caused by CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion in the HTT gene (>36 repeats). The pathology involves progressive neuronal loss primarily in the striatum and cerebral cortex. Clinical features include a triad of motor dysfunction (chorea, dystonia, bradykinesia), cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms. Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing. Management is symptomatic, with VMAT2 inhibitors for chorea. Emerging therapies include antisense oligonucleotides and gene silencing approaches.
historicalBackground: The disease is named after George Huntington, who described it in 1872 based on observations of affected families on Long Island, NY. The genetic cause (HTT gene) was discovered in 1993 after a decade-long collaborative effort. This was one of the first disease genes mapped using genetic linkage analysis and remains a model for understanding trinucleotide repeat disorders.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Oral votoplam shows dose-dependent slowing in PIVOT-HD
recentBreakthroughs.description: PTC Therapeutics' 28 April 2026 24-month PIVOT-HD extension analysis reported 52% slowing of cUHDRS progression at 10 mg and 28% at 5 mg in Stage 2 patients versus matched natural history, with sustained blood huntingtin lowering; a ~770-patient phase 3 (INVEST-HD) has begun.

recentBreakthroughs.title: First Huntington's gene therapy BLA filed with FDA
recentBreakthroughs.description: After a June 2026 Type B meeting in which the FDA accepted the three-year phase I/II analysis as the primary basis for accelerated approval, uniQure submitted the BLA for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130) on 2 September 2026, with a UK application filed in parallel. No approval decision had been issued as of 19 September 2026.

recentBreakthroughs.title: AMT-130 first therapy shown to slow Huntington's progression
recentBreakthroughs.description: On 24 September 2025 uniQure reported that high-dose AMT-130 produced a statistically significant 75% slowing of cUHDRS progression at 36 months versus propensity-matched external controls (p=0.003), with 60% slowing of Total Functional Capacity decline (p=0.033) and a mean 8.2% reduction in CSF neurofilament light.

recentBreakthroughs.title: Next-generation ASO therapies in trials
recentBreakthroughs.description: Following setbacks with tominersen, new antisense oligonucleotide approaches with improved selectivity are showing promise in early trials.

recentBreakthroughs.title: CRISPR gene editing advances
recentBreakthroughs.description: Researchers demonstrated successful reduction of mutant huntingtin protein using CRISPR-Cas9 in primate models.
